Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

(There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips."""
import sys

from kitty.cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface for kitty."""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import re
import sys
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import store
from kitty.money import (
    CENT,
    KittyError,
    allocate,
    fmt,
    from_str,
    parse_amount,
    parse_positive_number,
    to_cents,
)

_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]{3}$")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers


def out(obj):
    print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False))


def parse_currency(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if not _CURRENCY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError("invalid currency '%s': expected a 3-letter code like EUR" % text)
    return text.upper()


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        if len(text) != 10:
            raise ValueError
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("invalid date '%s': expected YYYY-MM-DD" % text)


def parse_id(text):
    if not re.match(r"^\d+$", text.strip()):
        raise KittyError("invalid ID '%s'" % text)
    return int(text)


def validate_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot contain ',' or '='")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError("member name cannot start with '-'")
    return name


def resolve_member(data, name):
    """Find a member by name, ignoring case; return the stored spelling."""
    wanted = name.strip().lower()
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.lower() == wanted:
            return member
    raise KittyError("unknown member '%s'" % name.strip())


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["base_currency"]:
        return "1"
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            "no exchange rate for %s; run 'rate set %s RATE' first" % (currency, currency)
        )
    return data["rates"][currency]


def convert(amount, rate):
    """Convert an amount to base-currency cents."""
    return to_cents(amount * Decimal(rate))


def parse_pairs(data, text, option, parse_value):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (member, value)."""
    pairs = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        if not item.strip():
            continue
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError("invalid %s entry '%s': expected NAME=VALUE" % (option, item))
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        member = resolve_member(data, name)
        if member in seen:
            raise KittyError("%s lists %s more than once" % (option, member))
        seen.add(member)
        pairs.append((member, parse_value(value)))
    if not pairs:
        raise KittyError("%s needs at least one NAME=VALUE entry" % option)
    return pairs


def parse_among(data, text):
    members = []
    for name in text.split(","):
        if not name.strip():
            continue
        member = resolve_member(data, name)
        if member in members:
            raise KittyError("--among lists %s more than once" % member)
        members.append(member)
    if not members:
        raise KittyError("--among needs at least one member")
    return members


def compute_shares(data, args, amount, base_cents):
    """Work out each person's share of an expense, in base-currency cents."""
    chosen = [
        opt
        for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent")
        if getattr(args, opt) is not None
    ]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError(
            "use only one of --among, --exact, --shares and --percent"
        )

    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.exact, "--exact", lambda v: parse_amount(v))
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                "--exact amounts add up to %s but the expense is %s"
                % (total.quantize(CENT), amount.quantize(CENT))
            )
    elif args.shares is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(
            data, args.shares, "--shares", lambda v: parse_positive_number(v, "share")
        )
    elif args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(
            data, args.percent, "--percent", lambda v: parse_positive_number(v, "percent")
        )
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError("--percent values add up to %s, not 100" % total)
    else:
        if args.among is not None:
            members = parse_among(data, args.among)
        else:
            members = list(data["members"])
        pairs = [(m, 1) for m in members]

    cents = allocate(base_cents, [w for _, w in pairs])
    return {member: c for (member, _), c in zip(pairs, cents)}


def expense_view(e):
    return {
        "id": e["id"],
        "date": e["date"],
        "payer": e["payer"],
        "description": e["description"],
        "amount": e["amount"],
        "currency": e["currency"],
        "base_amount": e["base_amount"],
        "category": e["category"],
        "shares": dict(e["shares"]),
    }


def payment_view(p):
    return {
        "id": p["id"],
        "date": p["date"],
        "from": p["from"],
        "to": p["to"],
        "amount": p["amount"],
        "currency": p["currency"],
        "base_amount": p["base_amount"],
    }


def sorted_events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order (then order of entry)."""
    events = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    events += [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    events.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[1]["date"], ev[1]["seq"]))
    return events


def balance_cents(data):
    balances = {m: 0 for m in data["members"]}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        balances[e["payer"]] += from_str(e["base_amount"])
        for member, share in e["shares"].items():
            balances[member] -= from_str(share)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = from_str(p["base_amount"])
        balances[p["from"]] += amount
        balances[p["to"]] -= amount
    return balances


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def cmd_init(args):
    if store.exists():
        raise KittyError("%s already exists in this directory" % store.FILENAME)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    store.save(store.new_kitty(currency))
    print("Started a new kitty in %s" % currency)


def cmd_member_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = validate_name(args.name)
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.lower() == name.lower():
            raise KittyError("%s is already a member" % member)
    data["members"].append(name)
    store.save(data)
    print("Added %s" % name)


def cmd_member_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = resolve_member(data, args.name)
    involved = [
        "expense %d" % e["id"]
        for e in data["expenses"]
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]
    ] + [
        "payment %d" % p["id"]
        for p in data["payments"]
        if name in (p["from"], p["to"])
    ]
    if involved:
        raise KittyError(
            "%s can't be removed because they appear in %s; remove those first"
            % (name, ", ".join(involved))
        )
    data["members"].remove(name)
    store.save(data)
    print("Removed %s" % name)


def cmd_member_list(args):
    out(store.load()["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    payer = resolve_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")

    base_cents = convert(amount, rate)
    if base_cents <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to be worth anything in the base currency")
    shares = compute_shares(data, args, amount, base_cents)

    expense = {
        "id": store.next_id(data, "next_expense_id"),
        "seq": store.next_id(data, "next_seq"),
        "date": date,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": str(amount.quantize(CENT)),
        "currency": currency,
        # The rate is recorded so later rate changes don't rewrite history.
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {member: fmt(c) for member, c in shares.items()},
    }
    data["expenses"].append(expense)
    store.save(data)
    print(expense["id"])


def cmd_expense_list(args):
    data = store.load()
    expenses = sorted(data["expenses"], key=lambda e: (e["date"], e["seq"]))
    out([expense_view(e) for e in expenses])


def cmd_expense_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    wanted = parse_id(args.id)
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["id"] == wanted:
            data["expenses"].remove(e)
            store.save(data)
            print("Removed expense %d (%s)" % (wanted, e["description"]))
            return
    raise KittyError("no expense with ID %d" % wanted)


def cmd_payment_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    sender = resolve_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = resolve_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    base_cents = convert(amount, rate)
    if base_cents <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to be worth anything in the base currency")

    payment = {
        "id": store.next_id(data, "next_payment_id"),
        "seq": store.next_id(data, "next_seq"),
        "date": date,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": str(amount.quantize(CENT)),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),

"""Money parsing, rounding and splitting.

All amounts are handled as Decimal and rounded to cents. Splits are done with
the largest-remainder method so the shares of an expense always add up to
exactly its base amount, and balances across the group always sum to zero.
"""

import re
from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")

_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$")
_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$|^\.\d+$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A user-facing error: printed as a message, exits with status 1."""


def parse_amount(text, what="amount"):
    """Parse a positive money amount with at most two decimals."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _AMOUNT_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(
            "invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number with at most two decimals"
            % (what, text)
        )
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_positive_number(text, what):
    """Parse a positive decimal number of any precision (rates, shares, percents)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number" % (what, text))
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    """Round a Decimal to an integer number of cents (half up)."""
    return int((value / CENT).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def fmt(cents):
    """Format integer cents as a string with two decimals, e.g. -2070 -> '-20.70'."""
    return str((Decimal(cents) * CENT).quantize(CENT))


def from_str(text):
    """Convert a stored two-decimal string back to integer cents."""
    return to_cents(Decimal(text))


def allocate(total_cents, weights):
    """Split total_cents in proportion to weights, returning integer cents.

    Uses the largest-remainder method: everyone gets the rounded-down share,
    then the leftover cents go to those with the largest fractional parts,
    ties going to whoever comes first. The result always sums to total_cents.
    """
    weights = [Decimal(w) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(weights)
    if not weights or weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount among nobody")
    exact = [Decimal(total_cents) * w / weight_sum for w in weights]
    floors = [int(e.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_DOWN)) for e in exact]
    leftover = total_cents - sum(floors)
    order = sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-(exact[i] - floors[i]), i))
    for i in order[:leftover]:
        floors[i] += 1
    return floors

    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(FILENAME))

    try:

            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")
        os.replace(tmp, FILENAME)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.unlink(tmp)
        raise

def cmd_settle(args):
    data = store.load()
    balances = balance_cents(data)
    order = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(data["members"])}
    creditors = {m: c for m, c in balances.items() if c > 0}
    debtors = {m: -c for m, c in balances.items() if c < 0}
    transfers = []
    # Greedy: repeatedly have the biggest debtor pay the biggest creditor.
    # Each step clears at least one person, so it takes at most n-1 payments.
    while creditors and debtors:
        creditor = max(creditors, key=lambda m: (creditors[m], -order[m]))
        debtor = max(debtors, key=lambda m: (debtors[m], -order[m]))
        amount = min(creditors[creditor], debtors[debtor])
        transfers.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": fmt(amount)})
        creditors[creditor] -= amount
        debtors[debtor] -= amount
        if creditors[creditor] == 0:
            del creditors[creditor]
        if debtors[debtor] == 0:
            del debtors[debtor]
    out(transfers)

    data = store.load()
    name = resolve_member(data, args.name)
    balance = 0
    rows = []
    for kind, ev in sorted_events(data):
        if kind == "expense":
            if ev["payer"] != name and name not in ev["shares"]:
                continue
            change = 0
            if ev["payer"] == name:
                change += from_str(ev["base_amount"])
            change -= from_str(ev["shares"].get(name, "0"))
            description = ev["description"]
        else:
            if name == ev["from"]:
                change = from_str(ev["base_amount"])
                description = "Payment to %s" % ev["to"]
            elif name == ev["to"]:
                change = -from_str(ev["base_amount"])
                description = "Payment from %s" % ev["from"]
            else:
                continue
        balance += change
        rows.append(
            {
                "date": ev["date"],
                "description": description,
                "change": fmt(change),
                "balance": fmt(balance),
            }
        )
    out(rows)

    data = store.load()

"""Money parsing, rounding and splitting.

All amounts are handled as Decimal and rounded to cents. Splits are done with
the largest-remainder method so the shares of an expense always add up to
exactly its base amount, and balances across the group always sum to zero.
"""

import re
from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")

_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$")
_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$|^\.\d+$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A user-facing error: printed as a message, exits with status 1."""


def parse_amount(text, what="amount"):
    """Parse a positive money amount with at most two decimals."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _AMOUNT_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(
            "invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number with at most two decimals"
            % (what, text)
        )
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_positive_number(text, what):
    """Parse a positive decimal number of any precision (rates, shares, percents)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number" % (what, text))
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    """Round a Decimal to an integer number of cents (half up)."""
    return int((value / CENT).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def fmt(cents):
    """Format integer cents as a string with two decimals, e.g. -2070 -> '-20.70'."""
    return str((Decimal(cents) * CENT).quantize(CENT))


def from_str(text):
    """Convert a stored two-decimal string back to integer cents."""
    return to_cents(Decimal(text))


def allocate(total_cents, weights):
    """Split total_cents in proportion to weights, returning integer cents.

    Uses the largest-remainder method: everyone gets the rounded-down share,
    then the leftover cents go to those with the largest fractional parts,
    ties going to whoever comes first. The result always sums to total_cents.
    """
    weights = [Decimal(w) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(weights)
    if not weights or weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount among nobody")
    exact = [Decimal(total_cents) * w / weight_sum for w in weights]
    floors = [int(e.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_DOWN)) for e in exact]
    leftover = total_cents - sum(floors)
    order = sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-(exact[i] - floors[i]), i))
    for i in order[:leftover]:
        floors[i] += 1
    return floors

import json

FILENAME = "kitty.json"


def new_kitty(base_currency):
    return {

        "expenses": [],

        "next_expense_id": 1,

        "next_seq": 1,

def exists():
    return os.path.exists(FILENAME)


def load():
    if not exists():
        raise KittyError(
            "no %s in this directory; run 'init CURRENCY' first" % FILENAME
        )
    try:
        with open(FILENAME, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError("could not read %s: %s" % (FILENAME, e))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not set(new_kitty("EUR")) <= set(data):

    return data

    """Write atomically, so a crash mid-write can't corrupt the file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(FILENAME))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=directory)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")
        os.replace(tmp, FILENAME)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.unlink(tmp)
        raise

        """Run a command; return (exit status, stdout, stderr)."""
        stdout, stderr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
            try:

            except SystemExit as e:

        return json.loads(self.ok(*argv))

    def setUp(self):

        os.chdir(self._tmp.name)

    def tearDown(self):
        os.chdir(self._old_cwd)
        self._tmp.cleanup()

    def run_kitty(self, *argv):
        """Run a command; return (exit status, stdout, stderr)."""
        stdout, stderr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
            try:
                status = cli.main(list(argv))
            except SystemExit as e:

        return status, stdout.getvalue(), stderr.getvalue()

        status, out, err = self.run_kitty(*argv)
        self.assertEqual(status, 0, err)

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips."""
import sys

from kitty.cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface for kitty."""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import re
import sys
from decimal import Decimal

from kitty import store
from kitty.money import (
    CENT,
    KittyError,
    allocate,
    fmt,
    from_str,
    parse_amount,
    parse_positive_number,
    to_cents,
)

_CURRENCY_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z]{3}$")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers


def out(obj):
    print(json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False))


def parse_currency(text):
    text = text.strip()
    if not _CURRENCY_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError("invalid currency '%s': expected a 3-letter code like EUR" % text)
    return text.upper()


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        if len(text) != 10:
            raise ValueError
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError("invalid date '%s': expected YYYY-MM-DD" % text)


def parse_id(text):
    if not re.match(r"^\d+$", text.strip()):
        raise KittyError("invalid ID '%s'" % text)
    return int(text)


def validate_name(name):
    name = name.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if "," in name or "=" in name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot contain ',' or '='")
    if name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError("member name cannot start with '-'")
    return name


def resolve_member(data, name):
    """Find a member by name, ignoring case; return the stored spelling."""
    wanted = name.strip().lower()
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.lower() == wanted:
            return member
    raise KittyError("unknown member '%s'" % name.strip())


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["base_currency"]:
        return "1"
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            "no exchange rate for %s; run 'rate set %s RATE' first" % (currency, currency)
        )
    return data["rates"][currency]


def convert(amount, rate):
    """Convert an amount to base-currency cents."""
    return to_cents(amount * Decimal(rate))


def parse_pairs(data, text, option, parse_value):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (member, value)."""
    pairs = []
    seen = set()
    for item in text.split(","):
        if not item.strip():
            continue
        if "=" not in item:
            raise KittyError("invalid %s entry '%s': expected NAME=VALUE" % (option, item))
        name, value = item.split("=", 1)
        member = resolve_member(data, name)
        if member in seen:
            raise KittyError("%s lists %s more than once" % (option, member))
        seen.add(member)
        pairs.append((member, parse_value(value)))
    if not pairs:
        raise KittyError("%s needs at least one NAME=VALUE entry" % option)
    return pairs


def parse_among(data, text):
    members = []
    for name in text.split(","):
        if not name.strip():
            continue
        member = resolve_member(data, name)
        if member in members:
            raise KittyError("--among lists %s more than once" % member)
        members.append(member)
    if not members:
        raise KittyError("--among needs at least one member")
    return members


def compute_shares(data, args, amount, base_cents):
    """Work out each person's share of an expense, in base-currency cents."""
    chosen = [
        opt
        for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent")
        if getattr(args, opt) is not None
    ]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError(
            "use only one of --among, --exact, --shares and --percent"
        )

    if args.exact is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(data, args.exact, "--exact", lambda v: parse_amount(v))
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                "--exact amounts add up to %s but the expense is %s"
                % (total.quantize(CENT), amount.quantize(CENT))
            )
    elif args.shares is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(
            data, args.shares, "--shares", lambda v: parse_positive_number(v, "share")
        )
    elif args.percent is not None:
        pairs = parse_pairs(
            data, args.percent, "--percent", lambda v: parse_positive_number(v, "percent")
        )
        total = sum(v for _, v in pairs)
        if total != 100:
            raise KittyError("--percent values add up to %s, not 100" % total)
    else:
        if args.among is not None:
            members = parse_among(data, args.among)
        else:
            members = list(data["members"])
        pairs = [(m, 1) for m in members]

    cents = allocate(base_cents, [w for _, w in pairs])
    return {member: c for (member, _), c in zip(pairs, cents)}


def expense_view(e):
    return {
        "id": e["id"],
        "date": e["date"],
        "payer": e["payer"],
        "description": e["description"],
        "amount": e["amount"],
        "currency": e["currency"],
        "base_amount": e["base_amount"],
        "category": e["category"],
        "shares": dict(e["shares"]),
    }


def payment_view(p):
    return {
        "id": p["id"],
        "date": p["date"],
        "from": p["from"],
        "to": p["to"],
        "amount": p["amount"],
        "currency": p["currency"],
        "base_amount": p["base_amount"],
    }


def sorted_events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order (then order of entry)."""
    events = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    events += [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    events.sort(key=lambda ev: (ev[1]["date"], ev[1]["seq"]))
    return events


def balance_cents(data):
    balances = {m: 0 for m in data["members"]}
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        balances[e["payer"]] += from_str(e["base_amount"])
        for member, share in e["shares"].items():
            balances[member] -= from_str(share)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        amount = from_str(p["base_amount"])
        balances[p["from"]] += amount
        balances[p["to"]] -= amount
    return balances


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- commands


def cmd_init(args):
    if store.exists():
        raise KittyError("%s already exists in this directory" % store.FILENAME)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    store.save(store.new_kitty(currency))
    print("Started a new kitty in %s" % currency)


def cmd_member_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = validate_name(args.name)
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.lower() == name.lower():
            raise KittyError("%s is already a member" % member)
    data["members"].append(name)
    store.save(data)
    print("Added %s" % name)


def cmd_member_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    name = resolve_member(data, args.name)
    involved = [
        "expense %d" % e["id"]
        for e in data["expenses"]
        if e["payer"] == name or name in e["shares"]
    ] + [
        "payment %d" % p["id"]
        for p in data["payments"]
        if name in (p["from"], p["to"])
    ]
    if involved:
        raise KittyError(
            "%s can't be removed because they appear in %s; remove those first"
            % (name, ", ".join(involved))
        )
    data["members"].remove(name)
    store.save(data)
    print("Removed %s" % name)


def cmd_member_list(args):
    out(store.load()["members"])


def cmd_expense_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    payer = resolve_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")

    base_cents = convert(amount, rate)
    if base_cents <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to be worth anything in the base currency")
    shares = compute_shares(data, args, amount, base_cents)

    expense = {
        "id": store.next_id(data, "next_expense_id"),
        "seq": store.next_id(data, "next_seq"),
        "date": date,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": str(amount.quantize(CENT)),
        "currency": currency,
        # The rate is recorded so later rate changes don't rewrite history.
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),
        "category": category,
        "shares": {member: fmt(c) for member, c in shares.items()},
    }
    data["expenses"].append(expense)
    store.save(data)
    print(expense["id"])


def cmd_expense_list(args):
    data = store.load()
    expenses = sorted(data["expenses"], key=lambda e: (e["date"], e["seq"]))
    out([expense_view(e) for e in expenses])


def cmd_expense_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    wanted = parse_id(args.id)
    for e in data["expenses"]:
        if e["id"] == wanted:
            data["expenses"].remove(e)
            store.save(data)
            print("Removed expense %d (%s)" % (wanted, e["description"]))
            return
    raise KittyError("no expense with ID %d" % wanted)


def cmd_payment_add(args):
    data = store.load()
    sender = resolve_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = resolve_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["base_currency"]
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    base_cents = convert(amount, rate)
    if base_cents <= 0:
        raise KittyError("amount is too small to be worth anything in the base currency")

    payment = {
        "id": store.next_id(data, "next_payment_id"),
        "seq": store.next_id(data, "next_seq"),
        "date": date,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": str(amount.quantize(CENT)),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_cents),
    }
    data["payments"].append(payment)
    store.save(data)
    print(payment["id"])


def cmd_payment_list(args):
    data = store.load()
    payments = sorted(data["payments"], key=lambda p: (p["date"], p["seq"]))
    out([payment_view(p) for p in payments])


def cmd_payment_remove(args):
    data = store.load()
    wanted = parse_id(args.id)
    for p in data["payments"]:
        if p["id"] == wanted:
            data["payments"].remove(p)
            store.save(data)
            print("Removed payment %d (%s to %s)" % (wanted, p["from"], p["to"]))
            return
    raise KittyError("no payment with ID %d" % wanted)


def cmd_rate_set(args):
    data = store.load()
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["base_currency"]:
        raise KittyError("%s is the base currency; its rate is always 1" % currency)
    rate = parse_positive_number(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    store.save(data)
    print("1 %s = %s %s" % (currency, rate, data["base_currency"]))


def cmd_balances(args):
    data = store.load()
    out({m: fmt(c) for m, c in balance_cents(data).items()})


def cmd_settle(args):
    data = store.load()
    balances = balance_cents(data)
    order = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(data["members"])}
    creditors = {m: c for m, c in balances.items() if c > 0}
    debtors = {m: -c for m, c in balances.items() if c < 0}
    transfers = []

    # Each step clears at least one person, so it takes at most n-1 payments.

        debtor = max(debtors, key=lambda m: (debtors[m], -order[m]))
        amount = min(creditors[creditor], debtors[debtor])
        transfers.append({"from": debtor, "to": creditor, "amount": fmt(amount)})
        creditors[creditor] -= amount
        debtors[debtor] -= amount
        if creditors[creditor] == 0:
            del creditors[creditor]
        if debtors[debtor] == 0:
            del debtors[debtor]
    out(transfers)

"""Money parsing, rounding and splitting.

All amounts are handled as Decimal and rounded to cents. Splits are done with
the largest-remainder method so the shares of an expense always add up to
exactly its base amount, and balances across the group always sum to zero.
"""

import re
from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")

_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d{1,2})?$")
_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$|^\.\d+$")


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A user-facing error: printed as a message, exits with status 1."""


def parse_amount(text, what="amount"):
    """Parse a positive money amount with at most two decimals."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _AMOUNT_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError(
            "invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number with at most two decimals"
            % (what, text)
        )
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def parse_positive_number(text, what):
    """Parse a positive decimal number of any precision (rates, shares, percents)."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not _NUMBER_RE.match(text):
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': expected a positive number" % (what, text))
    value = Decimal(text)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError("invalid %s '%s': must be greater than zero" % (what, text))
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    """Round a Decimal to an integer number of cents (half up)."""
    return int((value / CENT).quantize(Decimal(1), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def fmt(cents):
    """Format integer cents as a string with two decimals, e.g. -2070 -> '-20.70'."""
    return str((Decimal(cents) * CENT).quantize(CENT))


def from_str(text):
    """Convert a stored two-decimal string back to integer cents."""
    return to_cents(Decimal(text))


def allocate(total_cents, weights):
    """Split total_cents in proportion to weights, returning integer cents.

    Uses the largest-remainder method: everyone gets the rounded-down share,
    then the leftover cents go to those with the largest fractional parts,
    ties going to whoever comes first. The result always sums to total_cents.
    """
    weights = [Decimal(w) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(weights)
    if not weights or weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount among nobody")
    exact = [Decimal(total_cents) * w / weight_sum for w in weights]
    floors = [int(e.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_DOWN)) for e in exact]
    leftover = total_cents - sum(floors)
    order = sorted(range(len(weights)), key=lambda i: (-(exact[i] - floors[i]), i))
    for i in order[:leftover]:
        floors[i] += 1
    return floors

    if not exists():
        raise KittyError(
            "no %s in this directory; run 'init CURRENCY' first" % FILENAME
        )
    try:
        with open(FILENAME, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        raise KittyError("could not read %s: %s" % (FILENAME, e))
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not set(new_kitty("EUR")) <= set(data):

    """Write atomically, so a crash mid-write can't corrupt the file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(FILENAME))
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".json", dir=directory)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
            f.write("\n")
        os.replace(tmp, FILENAME)
    except BaseException:
        if os.path.exists(tmp):
            os.unlink(tmp)
        raise

I've added `expense edit ID` and the `--in CUR` option for `balances` and `settle`. All 40 tests pass, including 11 new ones for these features, and I tried both features by hand on a scratch kitty.

**`expense edit ID`** (in `kitty/cli.py`)
- It accepts the options you listed and changes only the ones you pass. The expense keeps its ID and its place in date order.
- If the amount or currency changes and you don't give a split option, the new amount is split equally among the people who shared it before. This applies even if it was split with `--exact`, `--shares` or `--percent`.
- If you only change things like the description or payer, the existing split is left exactly as it was.
- A split option on its own re-splits the current amount. `--exact` is checked against the new amount if you also give `--amount`.
- A new currency is converted at its current rate. If the currency stays the same, the rate saved with the expense is kept, so later `rate set` changes don't rewrite it. Switching to the base currency uses a rate of 1.
- Bad input fails the same way `expense add` does, and the expense is left untouched.

**`--in CUR`**
- `balances` and `settle` work out amounts in the base currency as before, then convert each one at the current rate and round it to the cent. The JSON shape is the same.
- A currency with no rate gives the usual "no exchange rate" error, and the base currency gives the normal output.

Decisions for you:
- **`expense edit 1` with no options** is an error ("nothing to change"). The catch is that a script running it would fail; treating it as a no-op that succeeds is a one-line change.
- **Confirmation message:** a successful edit prints `Updated expense 1 (Dinner)`, following the style of `expense remove`.
- **Tiny transfers:** a `settle` transfer that rounds to `0.00` in the target currency is still listed. That only happens when one unit of that currency is worth more than 50 base units, which is unlikely.
- **Rounded totals:** each amount is rounded on its own, so converted balances can be a cent off summing to zero.
